validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real, independently confirmed project. Pipeline & Gas Journal (2025-06-26, independent trade press) reported the Intensity Infrastructure Partners / Rainbow Energy Center JV to build a 344-mile ND gas pipeline in two phases; Intensity's own site carries the matching JV release (2025-06-26), the original Feb 2025 open-season notice, the Apr 2025 Phase II open-season notice, and a Jan 2026 FID announcement; EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook independently tracks 'Intensity Pipeline Project' (operator Intensity Infrastructure Partners, ND, intrastate, status Approved as of the 2026-05/08 releases) across 5 releases 2025-07 through 2026-08. Three independent origins (PGJ trade press, the company's own releases, EIA govt dataset) all agree the project exists and is moving forward. CLASSIFICATION: PipelineType=transmission is correct -- Intensity's own open-season/JV releases explicitly call it a 'natural gas transmission pipeline' (large-diameter, long-haul takeaway from the Williston Basin to in-state markets), not a gathering/lateral line; EIA's project_type is 'New Pipeline' (does not contradict). DUPLICATE CHECK vs P7783 (also 'Intensity Gas Pipeline', Washburn->North Dakota, 208 mi, 30in, 430 MMcf/d): P7782 and P7783 are NOT duplicates -- they are the two distinct, physically separate phases of one announced 344-mile project. The JV release (B) and the Phase II open-season notice (D) both state the project explicitly: 'Phase I includes construction of 136 miles of 36-inch natural gas transmission pipeline ... originating near Watford City, ND, and terminating near Washburn, ND. Phase II extends the pipeline 208 miles from Washburn to Casselton, ND, with a 30-inch segment.' P7782's recorded specs (Watford City->Washburn, 136 mi, 36in, 1100 MMcf/d) match Phase I exactly; P7783's roster line (Washburn->North Dakota, 208 mi, 30in, 430 MMcf/d) matches Phase II exactly. They interconnect at Washburn (which sits in southern McLean County, ND -- the interconnection point D names) rather than overlapping. This is the correct two-row modeling of a phased project, not a double-count; no merge recommended. See cross_row_leads for P7783's corroborating facts from these same documents.

validity.recommendation: do not use EIA 'Miles'=344 as a Length comparator for this segment row
validity.researcher_notes: EIA's own Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook (local file sources/eia_pipeline_projects/raw/, releases 2026-01 through 2026-08; Aug2026 release, sheet 'Natural Gas Pipeline Projects', Excel row 67) carries ONE 'Intensity Pipeline Project' row for the whole two-phase project, not one row per phase. From 2026-01 onward its Miles field is 344 (Phase I + Phase II combined), while its Additional Capacity and Diameter fields (1100 MMcf/d, 36in in the 2026-05/08 releases) actually describe Phase I alone -- an internal EIA inconsistency (aggregate length paired with a per-phase capacity/diameter), not a defect in this GEM row. GEM's segment-level modeling (P7782=Phase I 136 mi, P7783=Phase II 208 mi; 136+208=344, matching EIA's total) is correct and is the aggregate-vs-segment case the sweep instructions warn about. Recorded LengthKnown=136 mi stands, sourced instead from PGJ (A) and the company's own JV release (B), both of which state Phase I's mileage directly ('136 miles of 36-inch ... pipeline ... from near Watford City to Washburn'). Not proposing a Length change; flagging so a future pass does not 'correct' 136 to 344 off the EIA workbook. Three distinct origins, so high/independent stands on evidence rather than on assertion.]
